subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: If z₁ = −1 and z₂ = i, then find Arg(z₁/z₂).

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the argument of the quotient — what the two arguments are and what rule combines them.
insider_note: A quotient means subtract, and the order matters: Arg z₁ − Arg z₂ = π − π/2 = π/2. The one-line check −1/i = i confirms the answer before you write it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write the two arguments
steps.margin_note: First mark. −1 is on the negative real axis, argument π. i is on the positive imaginary axis, argument π/2.

recall.must_convey: That Arg(−1) = π and Arg(i) = π/2.
accept: the argument of minus one is pi and the argument of i is pi by two
arg minus one equals pi, arg i equals pi by two
minus one is on the negative real axis so pi, i is on the positive imaginary axis so pi by two
arg of minus one pi, arg of i pi by two

steps.why: Both numbers sit on axes, so their arguments are read from the picture: half a turn for −1, a quarter turn for i. No tan is needed.

steps.label: Subtract the arguments
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Arg(z₁/z₂) = Arg z₁ − Arg z₂ = π − π/2 = π/2, already in the principal range. Direct check: −1/i = −i/i² = i, argument π/2.
lines: Arg(z₁/z₂) = Arg z₁ − Arg z₂ = π − π/2
Check: z₁/z₂ = −1/i = −i/i² = i, Arg i = π/2.

recall.must_convey: That the argument of a quotient is the difference of the arguments, π − π/2 = π/2.
accept: the argument of the quotient is the difference of the arguments, pi minus pi by two equals pi by two
subtract them, pi minus pi by two is pi by two
arg of z one by z two equals arg z one minus arg z two which is pi by two
arguments subtract avuthai, pi minus pi by two equals pi by two
the quotient is i and its argument is pi by two

steps.why: Dividing complex numbers subtracts their arguments (and divides their moduli). The result π/2 is inside (−π, π], so it is the principal argument as it stands — and −1/i simplifies to i, which confirms it.
common_mistakes: Adding the arguments to get 3π/2 — that is the rule for a product.
Subtracting the wrong way round to get −π/2.
